questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display best compares counts across favorite snack categories?

feedback.text: Histograms group numerical values.
Scatterplots show two numerical variables.
A bar chart compares category counts.
Box plots summarize numerical data.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display lists categories and counts in rows?

feedback.text: A frequency table lists each category with its count.
Scatterplots show numerical pairs.
Histograms group numerical intervals.
Box plots summarize numerical distributions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is appropriate for two categorical variables such as grade level and club choice?

feedback.text: Dot plots show one numerical variable.
A two-way table organizes counts for combinations of categories.
Histograms display numerical intervals.
Scatterplots require two numerical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display could show each category as a part of a whole?

feedback.text: Box plots summarize numerical data.
Scatterplots show numerical relationships.
Histograms show numerical distributions.
A pie chart can show proportions for one categorical variable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Why is a histogram not appropriate for favorite color?

feedback.text: Responses can be counted by category.

answer.text: Favorite color is categorical, not numerical

feedback.text: Histograms need numerical intervals.

answer.text: Histograms are only for two variables

feedback.text: Histograms are for one numerical variable.
Scatterplots require numerical pairs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which variable is categorical?

feedback.text: Minutes are numerical.
Miles are numerical.
This is a numerical count.
Transportation method uses group labels such as bus, walk, or car.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A relative frequency table is useful because it shows what?

feedback.text: That is a scatterplot purpose.
Relative frequency compares category shares.
That is a box plot purpose.
That is a histogram purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display would be weak for category names only?

feedback.text: Bar charts compare category counts.
Frequency tables list categories and counts.
Pie charts can show category proportions.
Scatterplots require two numerical variables, not category names.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which question produces categorical data appropriate for a bar chart?

answer.text: How many minutes are spent on apps?

feedback.text: Minutes are numerical.

answer.text: Which app category is used most often?

feedback.text: App category is categorical and can be counted.

answer.text: What is the phone battery percentage?

feedback.text: Percentage is numerical.
Number of apps is numerical.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

When group sizes differ, what is often better than comparing counts only?

feedback.text: Relative frequencies make comparisons fairer when totals differ.
Group totals affect count comparisons.
Scatterplots do not fit two categorical variables.
Category names cannot be averaged.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display choice matches one categorical variable?

feedback.text: Box plots require numerical data.
Histograms require numerical intervals.
A bar chart can show counts for one categorical variable.
Scatterplots require two numerical variables.

Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

answer.text: They show how categories divide a whole

feedback.text: Each slice represents a category proportion.
That is a scatterplot.
That is a histogram.
That is a box plot.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which categorical display can compare counts with rectangular bars?

feedback.text: Box plots summarize numerical data.
Histogram bars represent numerical intervals, not category labels.
Scatterplots use points, not category bars.
Bar lengths or heights compare category counts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which is the best reason to label categories clearly?

answer.text: Labels turn categories into numerical values

feedback.text: Labels name groups; they do not make quantities.

answer.text: Labels replace the need for counts

feedback.text: Counts or percentages are still needed.

answer.text: Labels tell what each group represents

feedback.text: Clear labels prevent misinterpretation of category counts.
Labels do not establish causes.

CategoryCountDisplay fit

feedback.text: A histogram requires one numerical variable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

feedback.text: Frequency tables work for categorical data.

answer.text: Percentages account for different group totals

feedback.text: Percentages support fair comparisons across unequal groups.

feedback.text: Categories are still being compared.
Scatterplots use numerical pairs, not category percentages alone.
Percentages summarize data but do not prove causes.

feedback.text: A frequency table lists each club category and count.

feedback.text: That is bivariate numerical.

Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display could summarize yes/no responses by grade level?

feedback.text: Dot plots show numerical values.
Box plots summarize numerical distributions.

Grade level and yes/no response are categorical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

What does the height of a bar represent in a category bar chart?

feedback.text: Name length does not determine bar height.
Categories do not have medians.

answer.text: Count or frequency for that category

feedback.text: Bar height shows how many responses fall in the category.

feedback.text: Service names are category labels.
Hours are numerical.

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is best for showing percentages in categories out of 100 percent?

feedback.text: Scatterplots show numerical pairs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A student uses a bar chart for test scores 0 through 100 grouped by intervals. What would be more appropriate?

feedback.text: Grouped numerical intervals are represented with a histogram.
Pie charts are for categorical parts of a whole.
A two-way table is for two categorical variables.
A scatterplot is for two numerical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L04_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which justification best supports a bar chart for favorite sport?

answer.text: Favorite sport is numerical, and bars show intervals

feedback.text: Sport names are not numerical intervals.

answer.text: Favorite sport has two numerical variables

feedback.text: Only one categorical variable is described.

answer.text: Favorite sport is categorical, and bars compare counts by category

feedback.text: The display matches categorical data and the comparison goal.
Quartiles apply to numerical data, not sport categories.
